Architecture

Transactions, receipts and concurrency

A reliable reward is an idempotent durable effect, not a claim that networks deliver a message exactly once.

On this page
Command envelope and resultAtomic durable algorithmHow world claims stay atomicInventory capacity is a transaction invariantWorked concurrency casesRejection/error catalog

Command envelope and result

A mutation command carries CommandId (UUID), protocol/payload version, intended action, stable target/item IDs and expected revision. Account/character authority comes from the authenticated connection, not the asserted fields. The zone attaches its current SessionEpoch and service identity. Backend binds the command key to a canonical request hash.

Return Accepted with committed revision/receipt, Rejected with stable reason and no side effects, or Pending/Unknown while outcome is uncertain. On timeout retry the same key+payload or query status. A new key means a new action and must not be used to recover an uncertain old one.

Atomic durable algorithm

  1. Authenticate the zone/service and principal. Validate payload sizes/types/IDs and protocol. Begin a short DB transaction; never hold locks during an animation/cast wait.
  2. Acquire the command unique key or read the existing receipt. Same hash returns the existing outcome; different hash returns IdempotencyConflict. Concurrent identical calls wait/retry through the unique constraint.
  3. Lock current character session and needed character/container/source rows in a deterministic order. Verify epoch, lease owner, revision and live proof context. For two characters sort by UUID to avoid reversed lock order.
  4. Resolve authored definitions on the backend trusted catalog and recheck money, materials, binding, slot capacity, tool/profession/recipe gates and source claim availability. Compute the entire final occupancy/delta plan before modifying records.
  5. Generate server-side rolls/unique item IDs for this accepted transaction; persist outcome with source claim. Insert material/currency/XP/quest deltas, source depletion/stock state, ledger, result receipt and outbox event in the same database transaction.
  6. Commit. Only then update zone caches from the returned revision and replicate safe projections. Client audio/particles/UI completion are observers.
  7. If serialization/deadlock failure occurs, retry the complete transaction with the same command within a bounded service retry policy. If transport fails after commit, status/receipt query returns the committed result without rerolling.

How world claims stay atomic

A node Actor cannot participate in a PostgreSQL transaction. Its durable resource-generation row can. The zone first holds a transient reservation while progress runs; at completion the backend atomically changes that generation to Depleted and grants materials/XP. The zone applies the committed result and replicates depletion. Crash after commit reconstructs depleted state; crash before commit releases/cancels reservation and grants nothing.

Vendor finite stock, loot entitlement, craft recipe/owned materials and trade escrow use analogous durable rows. Do not deduct currency in a Blueprint, asynchronously request inventory addition, then call that atomic. A compensation workflow is needed only when a real separate authority cannot share the transaction; document states and reconciliation rather than assuming distributed atomicity.

Inventory capacity is a transaction invariant

A shared container_occupancy relation enforces one stack OR item per slot. Independent unique constraints in stack and item tables do not prevent one of each occupying the same slot. Plan consumed stacks and output slots together, enforce quantity/overflow bounds, and lock container capacity/revision. Binding/equipped/escrow locations cannot overlap.

Worked concurrency cases

CaseBefore / commit / expected
Two minersGeneration7 active; A and B request. One exclusive reservation wins; completion transaction marks generation7 depleted and grants2ore+5XP once. Other sees Busy or Depleted. Restart retains generation7 result; respawn creates generation8 at policy time.
Two vendor purchasesStock1, A/B wallets1000, price50. Stock row lock permits one purchase; winner950+1draught, loser1000+0. No negative stock.
Craft disconnectA has4ore2logs25currency. Commit consumes exact inputs and creates1hatchet GUID. Disconnect before reply; another-zone snapshot shows1result and one receipt, not another craft.
Quest claim replayReadyToClaim quest/cycle; unique character/quest/cycle reward claim. First commit100XP+200currency; replay returns same receipt after transfer.
Trade offers changeRevision5 accepted by A; B changes offer to6. Clear both confirmations. Settlement requires both accept6 and locks both characters/escrow/items/wallets atomically.

Rejection/error catalog

InvalidDefinition, Unauthorized, Forbidden, StaleSession, RevisionConflict, IdempotencyConflict, InsufficientFunds, InventoryFull, ItemChanged, EquipmentConflict, TooFar, NoLineOfSight, Busy, Depleted, StaleQuote, CastInterrupted, AttemptExpired, ZoneFull and TemporarilyUnavailable are proposed project reason codes, not Unreal built-in nodes. Map to localized user text; preserve command IDs for support.
